Q: How to use SQLite decimal precision notation A:

The SQLite documentation doesn't detail the SQL decimal type specification, because it ignores its semantics and falls back to its own custom numeric affinity scheme, as described on that same page.

In that case you can look up the original semantics in the SQL standard - or the Postgresql documentation, since Postgresql's documentation usually is very well written while Postgresql's coverage of SQL is quite high. The Postgresql documentation also goes into some length distinguishing between standard SQL syntax and its extensions. Also, FWIW, for some features SQLite even follows Postgresql's lead in adopting extensions.

In your quoted example


decimal(10,5)

shall be parsed as:

decimal(precision, scale)

Where

  • precision denotes the count of significant digits (i.e. count of digits before the decimal point plus count of digits after the decimal point), and

  • scale denotes the count of digits after the decimal

that can be stored in a column of such a type.

Note that SQLite, while it accepts that decimal type specification syntax, it doesn't implement its semantics. That means on insert it simply stores numbers without a decimal point as integers and numbers with a decimal point as IEEE floating point values.

IOW, SQLite simply ignores any precision and scale specifications and doesn't implement the decimal semantics.

Thus, in contrast to other databases, SQLite's decimal type is NOT well suited for typical accounting tasks, such as storing interest rates or computing on monetary values, due to well-known issues related to the binary floating point approximation of decimal fractions.

Q: Homebrew services. I can’t start the service and get "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error" A:

To see the real errors, you need to run the service without Homebrew (executable brew)

I had a similar problem, but instead of MongoDB, I could not start Apache (HTTPd).

brew services start httpd

Output:

Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error
Try re-running the command as root for richer errors.
Error: Failure while executing; `/bin/launchctl bootstrap gui/501
/Users/john/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.httpd.plist` exited with
5.
FAIL: 1

Unfortunately Homebrew doesn't show the user what causes this error. At first, I tried to use the tips from the answers in this thread, but neither reinstalling Apache nor unload -w/load -w helped. I also found nothing in the Homebrew logs. I decided to investigate Apache itself. To do this, I ran Apache without Homebrew:

/opt/homebrew/Cellar/httpd/2.4.51/bin/apachectl start

Output:

httpd: Syntax error on line 66 of /opt/homebrew/etc/httpd/httpd.conf: Cannot load /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so into server: dlopen(/opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so, 0x000A): tried: '/opt/homebrew/Cellar/php@5.6/5.6.40_3/lib/httpd/modules/libphp5.so' (no such file), '/usr/local/lib/libphp5.so' (no such file), '/usr/lib/libphp5.so' (no such file)
FAIL: 1

Then it was finally clear what was the reason why the HTTPd service was not starting. It turned out that after the PHP upgrade, the PHP version had changed, and I forgot to write the new PHP version in the Apache configuration file.

I quickly fixed this and Apache started up.

Q: Java multithreading and SWING A:

What you want to do is the standard way most designers would want to do it, that is, have a background worker class which is independent of the GUI.

Creating a class, MySwingWorker, which extends SwingWorker and which calls your background classes is the standard approach. You may want to create one or more dialog classes to wrap your usage of MySwingWorkers, depending on the complexity of your application.

Q: How do you install @hpcc-js/wasm in a way that integrates well with asset-mapper and importmap.php on Symfony? A:

Using @hpcc-js/wasm (Graphviz) in the browser — CDN vs Local Asset Mapper

@hpcc-js/wasm exposes Graphviz and other WASM-based modules that can be used in the browser. There are two main ways to include it in a Symfony app: CDN-only or local Asset Mapper.

Additionally, there is a subtle quirk with Symfony’s default importmap:require that can be confusing (arguably a bug).

1️⃣ CDN-only approach (zero local files)

You can import the package directly from a CDN without installing anything locally. The loader dynamically fetches Graphviz and the WASM modules.

Option A — jsDelivr “root” ESM:

<script type="module">
import { Graphviz } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@hpcc-js/wasm@2.33.0/+esm";

(async () => {
  const g = await Graphviz.load();
  document.body.innerHTML = g.dot("digraph { A -> B; B -> C; C -> A; }");
})();
</script>

Option B — jsDelivr explicit entry point:

<script type="module">
import { Graphviz } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@hpcc-js/wasm@2.33.0/dist/index.js/+esm";

(async () => {
  const g = await Graphviz.load();
  document.body.innerHTML = g.dot("digraph { Hello -> World }");
})();
</script>

Option C — esm.sh:

<script type="module">
import { Graphviz } from "https://esm.sh/@hpcc-js/wasm@2.33.0";

(async () => {
  const g = await Graphviz.load();
  document.body.innerHTML = g.dot("digraph { X -> Y; Y -> Z; }");
})();
</script>

Notes:

  • No local npm install needed
  • The loader dynamically fetches Graphviz and WASM
  • Versioning is managed by the CDN
  • Works entirely in the browser

2️⃣ Local Asset Mapper approach (Symfony-managed)

If you want versioning, fingerprinting, or offline support, you need to copy the files locally and point the import map to them:

npm install --prefix ./assets @hpcc-js/wasm
bin/console importmap:require @hpcc-js/wasm --path=assets/node_modules/@hpcc-js/wasm/dist/index.js

Usage in JS:

import { Graphviz } from "@hpcc-js/wasm";

// Tell the loader where to find the WASM file
Graphviz.wasmFolder = "/assets/node_modules/@hpcc-js/wasm/dist";

(async () => {
  const g = await Graphviz.load();
  document.body.innerHTML = g.dot("digraph { A -> B; }");
})();

Notes:

  • Fully managed by Symfony Asset Mapper
  • Fingerprinted assets (/assets/...)
  • Works offline

3️⃣ Important quirk / arguably a bug

If you run without --path:

bin/console importmap:require @hpcc-js/wasm
  • Symfony installs only a loader file wasm.index.js in:
/assets/vendor/@hpcc-js/wasm/
  • This loader does not include the helper modules or WASM files.
  • It is designed to work with absolute CDN-style paths:
/npm/@hpcc-js/wasm@2.33.0/dist/graphviz.js/+esm
  • Because Asset Mapper cannot resolve these absolute paths locally, the loader cannot work without a CDN.

💡 It’s confusing, because the default install creates a CDN-only loader. Using it locally without --path is not supported — arguably a bug in the way importmap:require installs this particular package.

4️⃣ Summary

Approach Local install Asset Mapper CDN WASM dynamic loading
CDN-only (jsDelivr / esm.sh) ❌ ❌ ✅ ✅
Local Asset Mapper ✅ ✅ ❌ ✅ (relative paths)
  • CDN-only: minimal, perfect for quick tests or demos
  • Local + Asset Mapper: full control, offline support, fingerprinting
